accessibility:
- **The WAI-ARIA Window Splitter pattern:** each handle is a focusable `separator` whose
  `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` give the size of the pane it speaks for, in
  percent, with `aria-controls` pointing at that pane.
- **Names:** a handle is named by its pane's `label`, so a screen reader says "Files, separator,
  25". A development build warns when a handle's pane has no `label`.
- **Orientation:** `aria-orientation` describes the line, so a handle between side-by-side panes
  is `vertical`, and one between stacked panes `horizontal`.
- **Keyboard:** Left and Right Arrow (or Up and Down when stacked) move a handle by `step`, and
  with Shift ten times as far. Home and End take its pane to its limits. Enter collapses a
  collapsible pane and brings it back. Right to left, the arrows follow the screen.
- **Pointer:** dragging works with a mouse, a finger or a pen, and a double-click puts the two
  panes beside a handle back to their default sizes.
- **Collapsed panes** are `hidden`, so nothing in them can be reached until they come back.
- **Focus ring:** Bulma's focus outline, inside the handle.
- **Target size:** the handle is 0.75rem across for a mouse and 1.5rem for a coarse pointer, which
  meets WCAG 2.5.8's 24px.
- **Forced colors:** the line and the grip are borders, which forced colors keeps, and an active
  handle is drawn in the system's highlight color.
- **Not live:** a resize announces nothing beyond the handle's value, which a screen reader reads
  on the focused handle as it changes.
summary: The `Splitter` component lays out two or more panes side by side or one above the other, with a handle between each pair to drag or move by keyboard. Each handle is a focusable `separator`, named by the `label` of the pane it speaks for. Sizes are percentages, so the server renders the layout the browser does, and `minSize` and `maxSize` also take `px` and `rem`. A `collapsible` pane shuts when dragged below half its minimum, and Enter on its handle shuts it and brings it back. It doesn't store sizes itself: keep them with `sizes` and `onSizesChange`.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes to apply.

props.name: children
props.description: `Splitter.Pane`s, two or more, each a direct child, with Fragments opened up. A handle goes between each pair. Changing which panes there are puts every pane back to its default size.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The way the panes run: side by side (`horizontal`) or one above the other (`vertical`).

props.name: height
props.description: The splitter's height. A number is pixels, and a string any CSS length. A vertical splitter needs a height to split.

props.name: sizes
props.description: Each pane's size, in percent, in order, adding up to 100. With it, the sizes are yours: update them from `onSizesChange`. Without it, each pane starts at its `defaultSize`.

props.name: onSizesChange
props.description: Called with every pane's size, in percent, whenever they change: on each step of a drag or a key, on a collapse and on a reset.

props.name: step
props.description: How far an arrow key moves a handle, in percent. Shift moves ten times as far.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper.

props.name: bgColor
props.description: Background color helper.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: One pane of a Splitter, sized by the splitter around it.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes to apply.

props.name: label
props.description: What the pane is, such as "Files". It names the handle that speaks for this pane, which is announced as "Files, separator, 25". That's the handle after it, or the one before it when only this pane, of the two beside that handle, can collapse. A development build warns when a handle's pane has none.

props.name: defaultSize
props.description: Its starting size, in percent of the room the panes share. Panes without one share what's left equally, and a total over 100 is scaled down.

props.name: minSize
props.description: The smallest it can be dragged: a percentage, or a CSS length in `px` or `rem` such as `"12rem"`. A length applies once the splitter has measured itself in the browser, so the server renders the default size.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: The largest it can be dragged, in the same units as `minSize`.

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Lets it collapse: dragging it below half its `minSize` shuts it, and Enter on its handle shuts it and brings it back at the size it had. It collapses only when the pane across its handle can take its room within that pane's `maxSize`, since a handle moves only the two panes beside it. A collapsed pane stays mounted, hidden, so it keeps its state.

props.name: collapsed
props.description: Whether it's collapsed, for a `collapsible` pane. With it, the state is yours: a drag, a key or a double-click that would collapse it or bring it back calls `onCollapsedChange` and leaves it as it is, and it changes when `collapsed` does.

props.name: defaultCollapsed
props.description: Whether a `collapsible` pane starts collapsed.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description: Called when a drag, a key or a double-click collapses it or brings it back, or, with `collapsed`, would. Not called for a change you made with `collapsed`.

props.name: children
props.description: What's in it. Content that scrolls belongs in a `ScrollArea`, so a keyboard can reach it.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper.

props.name: bgColor
props.description: Background color helper.

extraProps.name: id
extraProps.description: The pane's id, which its handle's `aria-controls` points at. The splitter makes one when there's none.
